flawed_step: 0120 | The claimed equivalence “∂²=0 if and only if (q+1)r=0 for all r∈R” is false for a q-complex having no faces of dimension 2 or higher. The argument in 0123–0129 proves necessity only when an appropriate pair W⊂₂U exists in X.
counterexample: Take q=2, R=ℤ, and the q-complex X=Gr(𝔽₂¹)={0,L}, where L=𝔽₂¹. Then C₁(X)=ℤ·L, C₀(X)=ℤ·0, and C_k(X)=0 for k≥2. Explicitly, ∂₁(L)=0 (the basis chain corresponding to the zero subspace), while ∂₀(0)=0 because the zero subspace has no codimension-one subspaces. Thus ∂₀∂₁(L)=0, and every other possible composite is also zero, so ∂²=0 on the entire chain module. Nevertheless, with r=1∈ℤ, (q+1)r=3≠0. Hence the asserted “only if” direction fails.
assessment_summary: The first definitive failure is step 0120: it omits a dimension/non-vacuity hypothesis. A complex with no 2-faces has ∂²=0 automatically, regardless of whether q+1 vanishes in the coefficient ring.
